messages:
sre-bot: PAGER: multigpu collective alarms firing for cluster-gamma. Symptoms aggregated: repeated NCCL timeouts, GPU OOMs, containers exiting with 137. PD alert INC-4821 created. root_ts: 2061122334
alice: grabbing console. Noticed surge of 502/500 on /generate for route rt/gamma-pp starting ~20:33 UTC. Pod restarts + elevated per-step latency.
carla: tailing logs from gpu-pp-7: 
```
[2026-03-15T20:34:10Z] ERROR NCCL: Call to ncclCommInitRank failed (errno 11)
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 14.00 GiB (GPU 0; 40.00 GiB total)
*** container exited with code 137
```
carla: also seeing NCCL timeout values reported ~30000ms in a few places.
dinesh: is this an all-TP layout or TP+PP mix? which model version?
alice: layout is TP=8, PP=2 on a 3-node placement (4 GPUs per host). We shipped a runtime kernel update ~2h before the spike.
kevin: cloud metrics show brief NIC errors and BGP route flaps on node-07 and node-09 around the same timeframe — could be a network instability triggering NCCL communicator failures.
maria: customer impact: two Dedicated tenants (cust-abb, cust-zen) reported elevated errors. Opening ops ticket OPS-798 and informing support.
alice: immediate mitigations I'm proposing:
 - cordon node-07 and node-09 to stop scheduling new PP ranks
 - drain affected PP pods and reschedule onto healthy hosts
 - rollout a rollback canary to previous runtime build if correlation holds
 - temporarily route heavy requests to a single-GPU quantized fallback for this route
 - set NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1 on the deployment to attempt recoveries
carla: executing drain on node-07 now: 
```
kubectl cordon node-07
kubectl drain node-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force\kubectl get pods -o wide | grep gpu-pp
```
carla: node-07 cordoned. Draining 4 PP pods; 2 recreated on other nodes, 2 stuck Pending due to affinity constraints.
dinesh: if rollback is needed I can coordinate. Who has the runtime package sha? @alice paste please.
alice: runtime build sha is ab12cd34 (deployed at 2045 UTC). Rollback target ef56gh78. Plan: rollback canary to 10 pods in region-1, monitor.
kevin: while draining, recommend reducing NCCL timeout to 20000ms and enabling NCCL_DEBUG=INFO. Also bump GPU driver watchdog timeouts to avoid premature kills.
maria: drafting customer-facing note: "We're investigating multi-GPU infrastructure errors causing increased latency and occasional failures for certain routes. We're applying mitigations now. No evidence of data leakage. Next update in 30m." Any edits?
alice: send that. ops-bot can post to status page.
ops-bot: STATUS PAGE: Incident INC-4821 acknowledged. Update scheduled +30m.
carla: drained node-09 as well; encountered one pod failing to start due to strict anti-affinity, scheduled into different AZ.
carla: recovered pod logs (new instance) show NCCL 'unreachable peer' events then OOM: 
```
NCCL ERROR Unreachable peer 192.168.12.7: timeout 30000
NCCL ERROR aborting
RuntimeError: ProcessGroupNCCL is not initialized (backend: nccl)
```
dinesh: hypothesizing timeline: transient network errors -> NCCL communicator degrades -> tensor buffering increases as ranks retry -> OOM -> container OOM exit -> restart attempts hit same communicator issues. Likely root cause: network plus runtime change interaction.
kevin: I'll run a staged repro in staging that injects packet loss on infra VLAN to see if our runtime changes remove previous NCCL fallbacks.
maria: support summary: cust-abb saw ~12% failure rate for /generate from 20:35-20:55 UTC; median latency moved from ~120ms to ~900ms. Marked high-sev for them and shared interim note.
alice: action items assigned:
 - dinesh: lead rollback canary to ef56gh78 and monitor NCCL logs (30m)
 - kevin: run packet-drop repro in staging and post results (45m)
 - carla: continue cordon/drain of unstable nodes and track Pending pods (ongoing)
 - maria: send customer updates + update OPS ticket (15m)
 - oncall-handoff: prepare for night shift takeover at 21:15 UTC if unresolved
oncall-handoff: I'll take handoff at 21:15 UTC. I'll validate mitigations and escalate infra-leads if the nodes keep flapping.
alice: starting rollback canary now: `kubectl apply -f runtime-revert-canary.yaml`
carla: canary pods are initializing. First few logs show reduced NCCL timeouts in the first 2 minutes.
kevin: preliminary repro results: with the patched runtime, NCCL appears to queue more under packet loss and is likelier to exhaust GPU memory; rollback candidate reduces queueing and memory pressure. Data point consistent with network-triggered OOMs.
dinesh: short-term runtime config tweak suggestion: reduce TP micro-batch by 50% for impacted route and enable per-request fallback to single-GPU to reduce per-rank memory.
alice: applying route-level micro-batch reduction for rt/gamma-pp: 
```
curl -X POST https://console.internal/api/v1/routes/rt/gamma-pp/config -d '{"micro_batch":0.5,"fallback_single_gpu":true}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN"
```
carla: config applied. New heavy requests now fall back to single-GPU quantized variant. Observed immediate drop in OOMs for those pods.
maria: customer update sent; asked for ETA. I replied 60-90 minutes pending validation.
oncall-handoff: if this persists at handoff, I'll request node-level NIC replacement and escalate to provider support.
alice: rolling summary: after rollback canary, node drains, and route fallback we observed error rate drop from ~12% -> ~1.3% over the last 10 minutes. Latency moving back towards baseline.
ops-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Mitigations applied (node drain, runtime rollback canary, route fallback). Error rate reduced; monitoring ongoing.
carla: leaving thread open another 40m for full validation across all TP shards.
dinesh: note for postmortem: likely root cause = interaction of runtime kernel change with transient NIC packet loss causing NCCL communicator degeneration and buffered tensors -> OOM. Postmortem action items: add canary tests simulating packet loss for NCCL, add automatic single-GPU fallback for PP heavy routes, and include NIC health checks in routing decisions.
alice: thanks all — I'll file postmortem and link INC-4821. Moving channel to monitoring mode.
